skill.name: security-report
skill.description: Generate DOCX security assessment reports with structured findings, risk ratings, evidence, and remediation recommendations.
skill.summary: Build consistent security reports for audits, vulnerability assessments, penetration tests, and compliance gap analyses.
skill.author: BytR-Ecosystems

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, or a formatted path in SKILL.md. The examples use Python document APIs and contain no Ruby or shell command execution. No intent-level security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - **Page breaks**: Add before major sections with `doc.add_page_break()`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 opens a fenced Python example. Lines 17-22 only import python-docx components and create a document heading, with no Ruby or shell execution.
Line 23 is the closing fence for the preceding Python example. It is Markdown formatting and does not execute an external command.
Line 31 uses backticks only to format the output path in workflow prose. It contains no executable statement or command interpolation.
Line 35 opens a plain Markdown block listing report sections. The block is documentation text, not Ruby or shell code.
Line 49 closes the report-structure Markdown block. The backticks are a formatting delimiter and have no execution behavior.
Line 55 formats the python-docx method doc.add_page_break() as inline code. It is a Python API call, not an external command.
Line 59 opens a fenced Python dictionary containing fixed RGB color values. The example performs no Ruby, shell, or subprocess execution.

content.value_statement: Security findings often become inconsistent reports that are difficult to prioritize. This skill guides structured DOCX reports with risk ratings, evidence, and remediation plans.
actual_capabilities: Guides DOCX report creation with the python-docx library.
Defines sections for executive summaries, scope, methodology, findings, roadmaps, and appendices.
Structures findings with identifiers, severity, CVSS, evidence, remediation, and references.
Maps five risk levels to fixed RGB colors for consistent presentation.
Recommends severity sorting, page breaks, bordered tables, and remediation timelines.
limitations: Does not scan systems, discover vulnerabilities, or validate supplied evidence.
Requires python-docx and an environment that can create DOCX files.
Does not include a complete CVSS calculation workflow.
Links to advanced reference files that are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Audit Report
use_cases.description: Turn approved audit findings into a structured report with an executive summary and remediation roadmap.

use_cases.title: Deliver Penetration Test Results
use_cases.description: Present tested vulnerabilities by severity with evidence, CVSS values, references, and recommended fixes.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Gaps
use_cases.description: Organize control gaps, risk ratings, and remediation priorities for leadership and control owners.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DOCX security assessment report for [organization]. Include an executive summary, scope, findings, and remediation roadmap using the supplied evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when findings and scope are already approved.

prompt_templates.title: Format Vulnerability Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a vulnerability assessment report from [findings]. Sort by severity and include identifiers, descriptions, evidence, remediation, and references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when raw findings need a consistent client-ready structure.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Penetration Test Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a penetration test report for [scope]. Add methodology, severity totals, CVSS values, detailed findings, and a prioritized remediation timeline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a completed penetration test with validated results.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Compliance Gap Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a compliance gap report for [framework]. Map each gap to risk, evidence, control owner, target date, and remediation priority.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced reporting across controls, owners, and deadlines.

output_examples.input: Create a report for four validated findings: one critical, one high, and two medium.
output_examples.output: A DOCX assessment with an executive summary, severity table, four ordered finding sections, and a phased remediation roadmap.

output_examples.input: Document access-control gaps against an internal compliance standard.
output: Executive summary describing the overall control risk.
Gap entries containing evidence, severity, ownership, and remediation.
Prioritized roadmap grouped by target date.

output_examples.input: Prepare a penetration test deliverable from approved technical notes.
output_examples.output: A structured report covering scope, methodology, risk distribution, evidence-based findings, references, and remediation priorities.

best_practices: Validate every finding and remove sensitive evidence before generating the report.
Use consistent severity criteria and confirm every CVSS value.
Assign remediation owners and realistic target dates before final delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated text as proof that a vulnerability exists.
Do not include credentials, personal data, or unnecessary exploit details.
Do not change risk ratings only to improve the executive summary.

faq.question: Does this skill perform a security scan?
faq.answer: No. It formats supplied, validated findings into a security assessment report.

faq.question: What output format does it target?
faq.answer: It targets DOCX documents created with the python-docx library.

faq.question: Can it calculate CVSS scores?
faq.answer: It can present supplied CVSS values, but this package does not include a complete calculator.

faq.question: Which report types are supported?
faq.answer: The structure supports security audits, vulnerability assessments, penetration tests, and compliance gap analyses.

faq.question: Can I customize risk colors?
faq.answer: Yes. Adjust the fixed RGB values in the generated document logic to match your reporting standard.

faq.question: How should sensitive evidence be handled?
faq.answer: Redact secrets and personal data, minimize exploit details, and follow the recipient's approved handling process.
